step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents Extreme Reach's Adbridge platform. Content Originators and Media Outlets access the system through an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) secured by an AWS WAF (FIREWALL). ELB routes user requests to the main application server tier (APP on EC2). Content originators directly upload ad assets to Amazon S3. The application tier queues asynchronous tasks into Amazon SQS queues, which are prioritized. Transcoding & Quality Control (QC TRANS) compute workers and Batch processing workers (BATCH) poll SQS for asynchronous workloads. Content delivery to media outlets occurs directly from S3 for broadcast ads, or via CloudFront CDN fed by S3 for digital video ads.

graph.name: Extreme Reach Adbridge Architecture
graph.notes: Extreme Reach processes around 80% of video ad traffic in the US using S3 direct uploads, prioritized SQS queues, EC2 transcoding/batch workers, and CloudFront CDN distribution.

nodes.name: CONTENT ORIGINATORS
nodes.notes: Advertisers and publishers uploading video ad assets via UI, API, or Java media uploader.

nodes.name: MEDIA OUTLETS
nodes.notes: Broadcasters and digital channels downloading broadcast-ready video ad assets.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer routing incoming API and web application requests.

nodes.name: FIREWALL
nodes.notes: Web Application Firewall monitoring and filtering promiscuous incoming traffic to the ELB.

nodes.name: APP
nodes.notes: Application server tier running front-end UI, API services, and system business logic.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 storing master video uploads and converted broadcast-ready files.

nodes.name: CLOUDFRONT
nodes.notes: CDN distributing digital video ad content directly to digital media outlets.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Amazon SQS priority queues managing asynchronous transcoding, QC, and batch workloads.

nodes.name: QC TRANS
nodes.notes: EC2 instances running video quality control and video transcoding tools.

nodes.name: BATCH
nodes.notes: EC2 batch instances executing background system maintenance and workflow jobs.

edges.notes: Content originators connect through ELB via UI, API, or Java agent.
Media outlets check into the system via ELB.
AWS WAF firewall monitors and filters traffic entering ELB.
ELB routes verified requests to application tier EC2 servers.
Direct upload of master ad assets to S3 via Java uploader or UI.
Application tier pushes asynchronous jobs into prioritized SQS queues.
Transcoding and QC worker instances poll SQS queues for work.
Batch processing instances poll SQS queues for background tasks.
CloudFront reads origin media assets stored in S3.
CloudFront delivers digital video advertising to media outlets.
Media outlets directly download broadcast video files from S3.
